title: Cognitive Development (Piaget)
summary: Piaget's theory: four stages of cognitive development (sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, formal operational), schemas, assimilation, accommodation and equilibration.
objectives: Describe Piaget's four stages of cognitive development.
revision: Piaget's cognitive development: four stages, schemas, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration.
traps: Piaget: sensorimotor → preoperational → concrete operational → formal operational.
Assimilation = fit new into schema; accommodation = change schema.

notes.t: A mental framework or concept that helps organize and interpret information.

i: Sensorimotor (0–2 years): object permanence, sensory and motor schemes
Preoperational (2–7 years): symbolic thought, egocentrism, no conservation
Concrete operational (7–11 years): logical thought about concrete objects, conservation
Formal operational (11+ years): abstract and hypothetical reasoning

notes.t: Fitting new information into existing schemas.
Changing existing schemas to fit new information.
The balance between assimilation and accommodation that drives cognitive development forward.
UGC NET frequently asks about Piaget's four stages, object permanence, conservation and egocentrism.

mnemonics.title: SPCFA
mnemonics.text: S — Sensorimotor (object permanence), P — Preoperational (egocentrism), C — Concrete operational (conservation), F — Formal operational (abstract reasoning), A — Assimilation/Accommodation
